design:
Tier 2: two gaps need new records, so a migration, and the operator's :8000 runs this checkout's migrations on its next restart. Hazard: a new table and, for the assignment history, a write on the task-update path. Rollback: both tables are additive and nothing reads them but the thread; dropping them returns the thread to what slice 1 shows. No backfill: a row invented for earlier deletions or assignments would put a claim in a history record that nothing observed (the rule TaskTransition already follows, models.py:914-930). The thread says plainly that history before the change shipped has no such knots. The acceptance drive is written and failing first on a dedicated trial Hub.

Decisions (author's choices, to confirm on review):
- Recommended gaps close at the cheapest honest level: show what exists (builds, carry-over checkpoints), record the two events whose loss is irreversible (deletion, reassignment).
- A deletion tombstone is one row per deleted task or document: kind, title, readable id, who deleted it, when, and the document it belonged to. It keeps no body, so it cannot leak what was deleted.
- Reassignment is one row per change of assignee (from, to, who, run when an agent did it, when), written in the same transaction as the change.
- New knot kinds are placed under the same parent rules as slice 1 (a build under its document, an assignment under its task, a tombstone under the document it left, else at the surface) and every one must belong to exactly one chapter (manager-chapters' every-knot-once), so the chapters job and its checks are told of the new kinds.
- The not-recommended candidates stay candidates: see the open question.

CONTRACT (names the tasks, tests and drive share; grounded in hub/hub/db/models.py, deletion.py, project_thread.py, chapters.py):
- Migration: revision 0169 in hub/hub/migrations/versions/ (latest is 0168_a_build_lands_as_one_pull_request.py), following .claude/rules' migration checklist; two additive tables, no data written by the migration.
- Table `deletion_records`: id, project_id, subject_kind ('task' | 'document'), title, readable_id, deleted_by ('operator'), placed_under (the owning document's id for a task, else null), deleted_at. The column is deliberately NOT named document_id or task_id: hub/tests/test_the_operator_can_delete_a_document_a_task_or_an_archived_agent.py:49 (`_REFERENCE`, test_every_reference_column_is_covered_by_a_cascade) fails for any column matching (task_id|document_id|...) that deletion.py does not list, and a tombstone must survive the deletion of what it names. If `placed_under` names a document later deleted, the knot goes to the surface.
- Table `task_assignee_changes`: id, project_id, task_id, from_assignee (nullable), to_assignee (nullable), changed_by ('operator' or an agent name), run_id (nullable), changed_at. Its task_id MUST be added to deletion.py's TASK_REFERENCES as ("task_assignee_changes", "task_id", DELETE): it goes with its task, and the tombstone is what remains. This relaxes nothing; it satisfies the guard above.
- Writers: tombstone in deletion.delete_task and deletion.delete_document, in the caller's session (routes DELETE /tasks/{task_id}, tasks.py:1708, and DELETE /documents/{path} in hub/hub/api/v1/spec.py:4801; a document's deletion writes one record for the document and one for each task that goes with it). Assignment change through one helper called from every site that writes Task.assignee (tasks.py:2123, 2458, 2464, 2577, 2726, 2730; builds.py:575, 594, 637, 1363; scheduler.py:1032; task_transition_service.py:739, 1024, 1188; run_divergence.py:754; run_task_binding.py:734; mender.py:425; already_built.py:227); see the open question on which sites count. A flow or the Hub acting without an operator or agent records changed_by 'hub'.
- Thread: knot kinds `deletion` (key `deleted:{record id}`, word 'Deleted', no link), `assignment` (key `assignment:{id}`, child of `task:{task_id}`), `build` (key `build:{build id}`, child of `document:{document_id}`, link to the build's card, reopenings as child knots `build:{id}:reopen:{n}`), `checkpoint` (key `checkpoint:{id}`, link to the checkpoint, parent the task bound to the successor conversation or the surface). Built in project_thread.build next to the existing leaf() calls; served unchanged by GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/thread (hub/hub/api/v1/thread.py:52). No new route, setting or SSE event. ROUTINE (project_thread.py:54) is not widened: these kinds are never folded away.
- Chapters: hub/hub/chapters.py surface_keys(thread) is thread.top, so a deletion or checkpoint at the surface joins it by construction; hub/tests/test_chapters_store.py and test_thread_feed_chapters.py are the existing guards to extend, none is relaxed.
- Task status path the drive walks: pending -> assigned -> in_progress -> completed -> under_review -> approved, with one reassignment while assigned, then DELETE of one task and of the document.
- Test files (named so the tasks share no path): hub/tests/test_deletion_records.py, test_task_assignee_changes.py, test_migration_0169_deletion_and_assignment_records.py, test_thread_history_gaps.py.

CURRENT   delete a task -> gone, and the thread has no trace it existed
PROPOSED  delete a task -> a 'Deleted' knot on the thread naming it, who and when; reassign it -> a knot under it; a build -> a knot under its document

open_questions.question: Which gaps to close? Candidates. RECORD (nothing exists today): (1) deletion of a task or document leaves no record; (2) reassignment of a task is overwritten in place; (3) changes to agents, runners, charters, project and manager-job settings are state, not events; (4) clearing traces leaves no event of its own. SHOW (records exist, thread does not read them): (5) builds, their stops and reopenings; (6) checkpoints that carried a conversation over; (7) stalls and the mender's actions; (8) run divergences and their retries; (9) task check runs, landings and landing batches; (10) main-red notices and main check runs; (11) spec rigor changes and edit proposals; (12) queued input the Hub withdrew or abandoned. Recommendation: close 1, 2, 5 and 6 (this document's requirements). 1 and 2 are the only irreversible losses; 5 and 6 are the answer to 'who built this and how did the work move between conversations' at no recording cost. Defer 3 (large, wants its own change and a settings-history design), 4 (the cost of losing a trace is stated in retention settings already), and 7 to 12, which the task story already draws per task, so a later slice can lift them to the thread cheaply once the operator has seen whether they want that much detail. The requirements are cut to the chosen set on approval.

Should the deletion tombstone be kept when a project is itself deleted, and should the operator be able to purge one (for example a title that should not persist)? Options: (a) kept until the project goes, no purge; (b) purgeable one by one. Recommendation: (a); the record holds a title and identifier only.

Which writers of Task.assignee count as 'changing a task's assignee' (reassignment-recorded)? The PATCH route is one of about twenty sites, including the flow's hand-outs (builds.py), the mender, run-task binding and transitions that move work between builder and checker, which would make the history mostly the Hub's own moves. Options: (a) every site, through one helper, with changed_by 'hub' for non-operator non-agent moves; (b) only the operator's and agents' explicit changes (tasks.py PATCH and MCP update_task). Recommendation: (a), since a history that skips the flow's hand-offs is not the history of who held the task; the thread can fold the Hub's moves as routine.

Is a checkpoint's successor conversation reachable from the Checkpoint row, so the carry-over knot can sit under the task its conversation was bound to and a checkpoint that started nothing add no knot (carry-overs-on-the-thread)? Checkpoint carries previous_checkpoint_id, lineage_id and covers_through_run_id (models.py:2236-2243) but the link to the successor Conversation was not traced; if there is none, the criterion's given cannot be built. Recommendation: confirm in the show task; if absent, the knot is placed by the checkpoint's own loop_id/lineage or at the surface and the 'started nothing' clause is cut.

problem: The roadmap says gaps are 'decided once they are visible' (spec/changes/red-thread-project-history-roadmap/spec.json, slice history-gaps). The thread is built by hub/hub/project_thread.py:403 from column reads of: SpecDocument, Task, Run, Conversation, AIJob, Loop, SpecRequirement, SpecDocumentEvent, SpecDocumentMerge, TaskTransition, TaskIntegration, RequirementEvidence, EvidenceReview, Question, PermissionRequest, Message, JobRun and vault entries (imports at project_thread.py:28-48). Two kinds of gap follow, found by reading, not by driving the thread. (A) Events that leave no record. Deleting a task or document removes its transitions, evidence, events, integrations and queued input and clears the pointer on what survives (hub/hub/deletion.py:6-13), so the thread, which never shows what has no stored record (slice 1, faithful), loses the work and the fact of deleting it together. A task's assignee is overwritten in place (hub/hub/api/v1/tasks.py:2123), so reassignments are not history: TaskTransition records status moves only (db/models.py:914), and Task has no revision table among the models. Changes to the agents, runners, charters and manager job settings of a project are state, not events: no table among the models records one. Clearing traces removes spans (hub/hub/traces.py:2531) with no event of its own that was found. (B) Records the thread does not show: Build (start, stop, stop_reason, level, people, reopenings; db/models.py:3385), Checkpoint (carry-over between conversations; :2194), Stall (:1329), RunDivergence (:1015), TaskCheckRun and TaskLanding/LandingBatch (:3454), MainNotice and MainCheckRun, SpecRigorEvent, SpecEditProposal (:2692), and a queued input the Hub withdrew or abandoned (InboundQueueEntry.abandoned_reason, :660). The task story already draws several of these per task (hub/hub/task_story.py:24-37) but the project's thread does not. The thread-from-records and manager-chapters documents are specified; this one is written before either is visible on the operator's data, so the list is the author's reading and is to be re-checked against the built thread.

requirements.rationale: A deletion is the one event after which the rest of the history cannot reconstruct it (hub/hub/deletion.py:6-13).
requirements.statement: Deleting a task or a specification document records, in the same transaction as the deletion, the kind, title and readable identifier of what was deleted, who deleted it, when, and for a task the document it belonged to; the record keeps no description, requirement text or evidence.

Each such record appears on the thread as a knot worded 'Deleted' that names what was deleted, who deleted it and when, placed by its recorded time under the document the task belonged to or, for a document or a task without one, at the surface; it links to nothing, since the object no longer exists.

Changing a task's assignee records the previous assignee, the new one, who changed it (the operator, or an agent's name and run) and when, in the same transaction as the change; setting the same assignee again records nothing.
Each reassignment appears under its task as a knot naming the old and new assignee and who changed it, in time order among the task's status changes and runs.

Each build of a document appears under that document as a knot recording when it started and who chose it, how it was driven, and, once it ended, how and why; a build reopened by a follow-up shows each reopening as a child knot, and the knot links to the build's card.

Each checkpoint that started a new conversation appears as a knot naming the agent, the trigger and the date, placed under the task its conversation was bound to or at the surface, and linking to the checkpoint.

requirements.rationale: The thread shows nothing without a stored record (slice 1, faithful).
requirements.statement: No tombstone or reassignment knot appears for anything that happened before this change was installed, and nothing is added to the earlier history by a migration.

A knot of any new kind belongs to exactly one chapter or, if recorded after the latest chapter version, appears after the chapters ungrouped, as every other knot does; a chapter version that drops or duplicates one is refused.

in_scope: A tombstone knot for a deleted task or document
A history of reassignments, as knots under the task
Builds and carry-over checkpoints shown as knots from records that already exist
Telling the chapters job and its checks about the new knot kinds
non_goals: Backfilling any earlier deletion or reassignment
Recording changes to agents, runners, charters, project and manager settings (candidate, not recommended now)
Showing stalls, divergences, check runs, landings, main notices, rigor events, edit proposals or withdrawn input (candidates, left to the open question)
Keeping the content of anything deleted
Any change to what the first two slices show

summary: Slice 3 of the red-thread roadmap. Reading the code the thread is built from, this lists the history the Hub never recorded or records and the thread does not show, and specifies closing the gaps recommended: a tombstone when a task or document is deleted, the history of who a task was assigned to, and builds and carry-over checkpoints appearing as knots. Which gaps to close is the operator's choice and is the open question; requirements here are for the recommended ones and are cut to whatever is chosen.
